newsitem.title: USA: Ahmanson disputes Great Western legal claim.
newsitem.headline: Ahmanson disputes Great Western legal claim.

text.p: H.F. Ahmanson & Co disputed Great Western's statement on Friday that California state banking laws would interfere with a merger of the two financial companies.
"This is simply not true. Great Western's conclusions are incorrect and simply a non-issue," Ahmanson said in a press release issued Friday.

Earlier on Friday, Great Western announced that state laws would require Ahmanson to file new regulatory applications, which could delay the proposed merger and the cost savings Ahmanson would hope to achieve.
Ahmanson launched its hostile bid for Great Western in February, which Great Western rejected in favor of a friendly merger proposal from Washington Mutual Inc.

"The application filed by Ahmanson with the Office of Thrift Supervision (OTS) was to acquire Great Western and not for the merger of the bank subsidiaries. Based on a written interpretation we received from the California Savings and Loan commissioner, we believe we can merge Great Western with out Washington bank," Ahmanson's said it its release late Friday.
"To avoid any question, we have contacted the OTS to advise it that we no longer expect to use our Washington bank as an immediate merger vehicle.
"We are confident that this matter will have no effect on the timetable for consummating our transaction of for achieving the cost savings we expect," Ahmanson said.
None of the companies, nor the regulatory agencies, was immediately available to comment on the dispute.
